1. Overview
FinRelief AI is a full-stack web application that helps a borrower understand their debt position,
estimate a reasonable settlement for each loan, and prepare a formal negotiation letter for the lender.
A borrower registers with their monthly income and expenses, adds loans through a guided form, and

then sees a dashboard of financial health indicators. From each loan card they can request a
settlement estimate or a negotiation letter written with the Google Gemini API, with a rule-based
letter used as a fallback when the AI service is not available.
The project is a working prototype. The core flow runs from sign-up to letter generation, while some
areas (described in Section 9) still need cleaning up before it can be called production-ready.
2. Problem Statement

2. Problem Statement
People struggling with loans often do not know how stressed their finances really are, what a fair
settlement might look like, or how to write a convincing request to a bank. Professional help is costly
and the process is stressful. The project explores how a small, approachable tool can give borrowers
clarity and a ready-to-send starting point for negotiation.
3. Objectives
(cid:127) Calculate simple, understandable financial health indicators from income, expenses and EMIs.

(cid:127) Estimate a settlement amount and risk category for each loan.
(cid:127) Generate a professional negotiation letter, with a fallback so the feature never fully fails.
(cid:127) Keep user data protected behind password hashing and token-based login.
(cid:127) Present everything in a friendly, conversational interface suited to first-time users.

4. Features Built So Far
The features below were checked against the code in the repository.
4.1 Accounts and security
(cid:127) Registration with name, email, password, monthly income and monthly expenses.
(cid:127) Passwords are hashed with Werkzeug; login returns a JWT that expires after 120 minutes.
(cid:127) Protected pages in the front end, and automatic sign-out when the server returns an unauthorised
response.
4.2 Financial health dashboard

response.
4.2 Financial health dashboard
(cid:127) Four indicators: stress level, monthly surplus, EMI-to-income ratio and debt-to-income ratio.
(cid:127) Indicators are recalculated each time the dashboard loads and saved to the user's profile.
(cid:127) Loan cards show lender, type, outstanding amount, EMI, interest rate and any overdue months,
with amounts in rupees.
4.3 Guided loan entry
(cid:127) Six-step form with a progress bar and friendly prompts for lender, type, balance, rate, EMI and

overdue months.
(cid:127) Seven loan types: Personal, Home, Car, Education, Business, Credit Card and Other.
4.4 Settlement prediction
(cid:127) One click per loan returns a suggested settlement, a risk category and the amount that could be
saved.
(cid:127) The result is stored in the database for later reference.
4.5 AI negotiation letters
(cid:127) A prompt built from the borrower's profile and the loan details is sent to Google Gemini to draft a
formal letter that also asks for a No Dues Certificate.

formal letter that also asks for a No Dues Certificate.
(cid:127) If the API key is missing or the call fails, a rule-based template letter is returned instead; the front
end also holds its own backup letter.
(cid:127) Letters can be copied or downloaded as a text file, and each generated letter is saved in an AI
history table.
4.6 Financial advisor page
(cid:127) Plain-language tips based on surplus, EMI ratio, DTI, overdue loans, payoff time and an estimate
of possible savings.

of possible savings.

(cid:127) Four-slide onboarding introduction and a dark, card-based theme with a conversational tone.

documentation, demonstration), six screenshots and a recorded demo video.

8. How the Numbers Are Calculated
The calculations are simple rules kept in a separate financial engine module, which makes them
easy to read and change.
Measure Rule used in the code
Monthly surplus Income minus expenses minus total EMI
EMI ratio Total EMI divided by income, as a percentage
DTI ratio (Expenses plus total EMI) divided by income, as a percentage
Stress level High above 40% EMI ratio, Medium above 20%, otherwise Low

Stress level High above 40% EMI ratio, Medium above 20%, otherwise Low
Settlement discount Base 20%. Add 5% for 1-3 overdue months, 10% for 4-6, 15% for over 6. Add 5%
more for personal loans.
Risk category High above 3 overdue months, Medium for 1-3, Low when nothing is overdue
Settlement figures are rule-based estimates, not guarantees, and the letters are drafts rather than legal or financial
advice.

1. Overview
The APSRTC Smart Yatra Assistant brings schedules, a live bus map, passenger safety tools, an AI
helper and full voice control into one web application. It is designed first for accessibility: six languages,
a high-contrast mode, three text sizes and hands-free voice navigation for visually impaired commuters.

The prototype already covers the main journey, from finding a stop and tracking a bus to recovering
from a missed bus and reaching help in an emergency. It is not yet a finished product; the map, the AI
agent and offline use need further work, as described in this document.
2. Problem Statement
Bus travel remains the main mode of public transport for a very large number of people in Andhra
Pradesh, yet everyday commuters still face avoidable difficulties: little reliable information about where a

bus is, language barriers in apps, limited support for visually impaired passengers, no easy way to
share a journey with family for safety, and no guidance when a bus is missed. The project explores how
one lightweight app can address several of these gaps together.
3. Objectives
(cid:127) Make bus travel information easier to reach for all passengers, including those with low vision.
(cid:127) Offer the interface in English, Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam.

(cid:127) Give commuters a simple safety net through an arrival check-in that escalates to an SOS message.
(cid:127) Help passengers recover quickly when a bus is missed, with alternative transport and budget advice.
(cid:127) Provide a clear path to official helplines and a formal grievance letter.

6. Application Flow
(cid:127) The commuter opens the app, picks a language and, if needed, high contrast or voice control.
(cid:127) The map shows stations and buses; the nearest-stop tool or a city hub shortcut narrows the view.

(cid:127) The assistant answers route, fare and concession questions and advises when a bus is missed.
(cid:127) For safety, the commuter arms a trip; the check-in either closes safely or sends the SOS package.
(cid:127) For complaints, the letter generator prepares a formal message ready to send.

11. Expected Outcome
By mid-2027 the aim is a dependable, installable app that works on weak networks, shows accurate
maps, answers commuter questions consistently and can alert a trusted contact without relying on the
commuter's phone. The later phases depend on official data access and are treated as stretch goals.
12. Conclusion

12. Conclusion
The project already demonstrates a broad and accessible idea for AP commuters. Its honest status is a
strong prototype with clear weaknesses in maps, AI behaviour and offline use. Fixing those three areas
is the first priority, and the roadmap is ordered to do exactly that before adding new features.
